vulnerable_statements.reason: The firmware-shared Command DB region is mapped write-back cacheable. This region is shared with remote processors and protected by the hypervisor/XPU, so cacheable mapping allows speculative accesses and cache maintenance against memory that must not be accessed that way, which can cause faults or stale/inconsistent data. The mapping is also never released: it is not device-managed and is not unmapped on the later error path.
When the magic check fails (line 21), the function returns without calling memunmap(cmd_db_header), so the mapping leaks. cmd_db_header also keeps pointing at the invalid mapping as a global.

suggested_fix: Map the region with MEMREMAP_WC (non-cacheable, as other qcom shared-memory drivers do) instead of MEMREMAP_WB. Use devm_memremap() so the mapping is freed automatically if probe fails, or else call memunmap() and set cmd_db_header to NULL before returning on the magic-mismatch error path.
